newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania parliament approves road, rail concessions.
newsitem.headline: Romania parliament approves road, rail concessions.

text.p: The Romanian parliament's lower house has approved a draft law awarding road and railway concessions in a bid to improve the country's infrastructure, a parliamentary spokesman said on Thursday.
"The draft law, which has already cleared the upper Senate, is now awaiting presidential approval," spokesman Ovidiu Marian said of Wednesday's vote.
Romania's roads and railways, battered by years of neglect under the ousted communists, are now further deteriorating due to lack of funds for repairs and growing traffic.

According to Transport Ministry sources, two-thirds of the total road network of 14,500 km (9,000 miles) are in need of immediate repairs, as are some 900 km (550 miles) of the rail network, which extends over 11,000 km (7,000 miles).

The bill says concessions will be awarded for a period of up to 20 years and for longer periods to investors wishing to build or repair motorways or rail lines. But a time limit of 49 years was imposed for longer-term projects.
Last year, Romania announced plans to award concessions worth $1.8 billion strictly to foreign investors as part of a broader programme to improve the road network.
The country's railway authority SNCFR also plans concessions of railway sectors to pull in domestic and foreign capital to upgrade rail infrastructure.

SNCFR said last month it had worked out plans for concessions covering three rail sectors, including electrification, upgrading and double-tracking and intended to offer concessions for another 14 sectors in the future.
Official estimates show Romania needs around $30 billion to upgrade and develop its road, rail, air and sea transport by the year 2005. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
